title: Trump: French researcher is first-known case of denied entry to U.S. of anti-Trump travelers
description_short: Trump: French researcher is first-known case of denied entry to U.S. of anti-Trump travelers
description_medium: TrumpFile reported that a French space researcher was detained at a Houston airport, had devices searched and was sent back to Europe. It relayed Le Monde’s account that messages criticizing Trump administration research policies were found. The page separately names French minister Philippe Baptiste in a statement, leaving unclear whether he was the traveler or a commentator.
description_long: TrumpFile’s March 9, 2025 timeline says a French space researcher was questioned at a Houston airport, had a work computer and personal phone searched, and was sent back to Europe the following day. It relays a rough translation of Le Monde reporting that messages criticizing the Trump administration’s research policy were found on the devices and that the researcher was accused of expressing hostility toward Trump. The timeline says the equipment was reportedly confiscated. It also quotes a statement from Philippe Baptiste, France’s minister for higher education and research, regretting the U.S. authorities’ decision, and notes that he had published an open letter urging U.S. scientists to relocate to France. The page’s opening identifies Baptiste as the person detained, while the translated passage describes a space researcher and the minister appears separately as the source of a comment. Without the underlying Le Monde report, the identity and roles cannot be reconciled. The incident should remain attributed until that distinction is clear.
subcategory: Researcher entry and device search at U.S. border
organization_tags: French Ministry of Higher Education and Research

preserved_fields.title: Trump: French researcher is first-known case of denied entry to U.S. of anti-Trump travelers
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: French researcher is first-known case of denied entry to U.S. of anti-Trump travelers

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile page, which relays a rough translation of Le Monde. It reports a French researcher’s detention and return but also names Philippe Baptiste as a minister commenting on the decision; the page does not make their identities and roles clear. Proposed correction: verify the traveler’s identity and distinguish that person from Baptiste before retaining the headline’s identification.
proposed_correction: French Researcher Reportedly Turned Back After Device Search; Identity Needs Clarification

title: Trump orders removal of Black History from Smithsonian
description_short: Trump orders removal of Black History from Smithsonian
description_medium: Trump’s March 27, 2025 executive order, “Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History,” criticized Smithsonian presentations about race and named “The Shape of Power.” It assigned the vice president a role in reviewing exhibitions and allowed potential changes, but the linked page does not document that the exhibit or Black-history materials were removed.
description_long: On March 27, 2025, Trump signed the executive order “Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History.” The order criticized the Smithsonian Institution for what it called divisive, race-centered ideology and cited “The Shape of Power: Stories of Race and American Sculpture,” an exhibition examining race in the United States. According to the linked account, the order gave the vice president a role in reviewing exhibitions and potentially eliminating those the administration considered inconsistent with its view of American history. It also directed the vice president to work with Congress on Smithsonian appropriations, called for reinstating monuments removed since 2020, and restricted descriptions of historical figures that condemn them. These directives place pressure on how the Smithsonian and federal monuments present race and national history. The source does not show that the named exhibition was taken down or that Black-history displays were removed. The documented event is an executive order setting review and policy requirements, not proof that the threatened removals had already occurred. The headline’s claim that Trump ordered removal of Black history therefore needs revision.
subcategory: Executive order on Smithsonian exhibits and historical presentation

preserved_fields.title: Trump orders removal of Black History from Smithsonian
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump orders removal of Black History from Smithsonian

notes: The linked TrumpFile page identifies the order and exhibition, and describes review authority and potential changes. It does not document that an exhibit or Black-history material was removed. Proposed correction: describe the order’s review and presentation requirements, not completed removal.
proposed_correction: Trump Order Directs Smithsonian Exhibit Review and Changes to Historical Presentation

title: deployed troops to Portland, Oregon claiming the city was filled with "domestic
description_short: President Trump deployed troops to Portland, Oregon claiming the city was filled with "domestic terrorists" and describing it as "war-ravaged"
description_medium: On September 27, 2025, Trump said he was directing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to send troops to Portland to protect ICE facilities, which he described as under attack by “domestic terrorists.” NBC News reported that Pentagon officials were not aware of a new deployment order and lacked details about any operation. The article documents a directive and public claims, not troops already deployed.
description_long: On September 27, 2025, Trump wrote on Truth Social that he was directing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to provide troops to Portland, Oregon, to protect Immigration and Customs Enforcement facilities. He described the city as “war ravaged,” claimed the facilities were under attack by Antifa and other “domestic terrorists,” and said he was authorizing “Full Force” if necessary without explaining what that meant. NBC News reported that Pentagon officials were surprised by the post and had no information about an order, mission scope, or whether National Guard or active-duty forces would be used. A Pentagon spokesperson said the department was ready to support DHS operations at the president’s direction. Portland officials urged residents to remain calm and said they had not requested troops. The reporting records Trump’s direction and the disputed descriptions he used; it does not establish that a deployment had occurred at publication. The title and short field say troops were deployed, while the article supports only an announced directive at that point. The status of any later deployment is not established by this linked report.
subcategory: Presidential troop directive for Portland ICE facilities

preserved_fields.title: deployed troops to Portland, Oregon claiming the city was filled with "domestic
preserved_fields.description_short: President Trump deployed troops to Portland, Oregon claiming the city was filled with "domestic terrorists" and describing it as "war-ravaged"

notes: I read the linked NBC News report. It says Trump directed Hegseth to provide troops, while Pentagon officials told NBC they knew of no new order and had no deployment details; Portland officials said they had not requested troops. The populated short description’s “deployed” wording is not established by this report. Proposed correction: change the title and short text to say Trump directed or announced a troop deployment.
proposed_correction: Trump Directs Hegseth to Provide Troops to Portland; Deployment Not Confirmed in Report

title: Trump: Pete Hegseth and lawyer lied to White House about leaks
description_short: Trump: Pete Hegseth and lawyer lied to White House about leaks
description_medium: The Guardian reported a White House–Pentagon rift after Pete Hegseth’s lawyer, Tim Parlatore, said a warrantless wiretap found classified documents on an aide’s phone, then denied that a wiretap occurred. The linked account says the leak inquiry and related firings were disputed. Its headline’s claim that Hegseth and the lawyer lied is not established by the supplied account.
description_long: On May 27, 2025, reporting described a rift between the White House and Pentagon over an investigation into leaks at the Defense Department. Tim Parlatore, Hegseth’s personal lawyer, had been assigned to oversee the inquiry. He reportedly told White House advisers that a warrantless wiretap had found classified material on the phone of Dan Caldwell, then a senior Hegseth adviser, but later denied that a wiretap had taken place and said information came from Pentagon officials. The TrumpFile timeline says Caldwell, Colin Carroll and Darin Selnick were fired at the request of Joe Kasper, a former chief of staff with ties to Parlatore, and that investigators had not initially focused on those aides. Parlatore’s account and the timing of the firings became points of dispute; the source also says the investigation was transferred to Deputy Defense Secretary Stephen Feinberg. This reporting documents conflicting accounts and internal personnel tensions. It does not establish that Hegseth or Parlatore deliberately lied to the White House, as the headline states. The claim should remain attributed unless additional evidence resolves the contradiction.
subcategory: Pentagon leak investigation and disputed wiretap account
organization_tags: Air Force Office of Special Investigations

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Pete Hegseth and lawyer lied to White House about leaks
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Pete Hegseth and lawyer lied to White House about leaks

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile page, which summarizes Guardian and New Republic reporting. It says Parlatore first described a warrantless wiretap and later denied one, and that the inquiry shifted to Deputy Defense Secretary Stephen Feinberg. This establishes a disputed account, not deliberate lying by Hegseth or counsel. Proposed correction: headline the conflict over the leak investigation and wiretap claim.
proposed_correction: Pentagon Leak Inquiry: White House Questions Parlatore’s Wiretap Account

title: Trump: Harvard scientist released by ICE after 4 months illegal detention
description_short: Trump: Harvard scientist released by ICE after 4 months illegal detention
description_medium: A federal judge in Vermont released Harvard researcher Kseniia Petrova on bond after about four months in immigration custody and ruled that ICE’s detention was unlawful. The linked account says the case involved frog-embryo samples she brought from France and a criminal smuggling charge. It does not connect Trump personally to her detention or release.
description_long: On June 12, 2025, a federal judge in Vermont released Harvard researcher Kseniia Petrova from immigration custody on bond after roughly four months of detention. The linked account says the judge also ruled that ICE’s detention of Petrova was unlawful. Petrova, a Russian national, had been detained after returning from France with frog-embryo samples intended for research; she faced a criminal charge of smuggling the samples into the United States. Petrova said she did not realize the materials needed to be declared, while the Department of Homeland Security said she failed to declare or misrepresented them. Colleagues and academics testified about her research at Harvard and its potential contribution to cancer treatment. The report describes competing accounts and a court’s decision on detention, not a final resolution of the criminal charge. It does not report that Trump personally ordered the detention or release. The title’s “Trump:” framing therefore implies a connection this source does not document; a corrected entry should focus on Petrova, the court ruling and the immigration detention.
subcategory: Unlawful immigration detention and bond release

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Harvard scientist released by ICE after 4 months illegal detention
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Harvard scientist released by ICE after 4 months illegal detention

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile page, which reproduces AP reporting. It says a Vermont judge released Petrova on bond and ruled ICE’s detention unlawful; it describes competing accounts about the frog-embryo samples and a pending criminal charge. It does not connect Trump personally to the detention. Proposed correction: remove “Trump:” and identify the detention ruling and release.
proposed_correction: Judge Rules ICE Detention of Harvard Researcher Kseniia Petrova Unlawful
